findings.text: follow-on: the reviewed manifest omits the baseline_suite arm entirely and its baseline.log header reads 'revision=5ec8b0ee... tree=<worktree>' without recording that the tree carried an intermediate reviewed source. Reconstructed as the true base SOURCE (5ec8b0eed5637fffa6990f3194150bf52b01cad7) plus the reviewed test file, the arm is a collection ImportError (cannot import name 'acquire_host_session'), not the recorded 1-failed run -- so the recorded baseline is an intermediate commit, not the declared base revision, and the added-failure derivation rests on the all-green after arm alone.

follow-on: the one owner of the bound lives in ssh_worker.py, but executor.py reaches into its private surface -- imports _session_permit and reads pool._owner_loop, pool._started and pool._closed -- so the cross-module contract is carried by names with a leading underscore; a rename or a change to pool internals breaks the executor bridge silently at runtime rather than at import.

follow-on: test_limited_host_serializes_calls_and_unlimited_host_overlaps asserts peak == 2 exactly for the unlimited host behind a 0.05s sleep; the overlap of two 0.05s sleeps is a scheduling race, so a stall that serialises the two thread starts would redden a correct change. The async counterpart deliberately uses 'peak >= 2' for the same condition, so the strict equality is applied only to the synchronous arm.

item_verdicts.call_sites: The bound has one owner in ssh_worker.py and five call sites consume it: run_command, run_script_via_stdin, run_python_script and async_run_python_script in executor.py take a permit from _session_permit and route through an open pool when one exists, and SSHWorker.start takes one permit per pool worker for the worker's life (released on close/kill).
item_verdicts.diff: Three commits against 5ec8b0ee: 96bd503a adds the _host_sessions registry, the permit acquisition in SSHWorker, pool sizing, the run_subprocess bridge and executor routing (+~360/-73 across executor.py, ssh_worker.py, tools.py, the schema and jt-60sa.yaml plus a 231-line test file); 4120090e registers the limit for direct executor callers on first resolution and hardens pool discovery; a0bbbfc4 is the evidence-anchor doc commit.
item_verdicts.done_when: All three done-when clauses are carried: test_limited_host_serializes_calls_and_unlimited_host_overlaps shows limited peak 1 and unlimited peak 2; test_async_and_threaded_calls_share_the_host_limit shows a mixed async/threaded gather peaking at 1 on a limited host and >=2 on an unlimited one; test_facility_declares_one_session shows get_facility('jt-60sa')['ssh_max_sessions'] == 1 and validate_facility_config('jt-60sa') == [].
item_verdicts.goal: §60 asks for an optional per-facility ssh_max_sessions, set to 1 for JT-60SA, with one owner beside the pool registry, pools sized to the limit, each worker holding one session for its life, per-call paths taking a session from the same bound and routing through an open pool, unlimited hosts unchanged, and the process-local scope stated in code. ssh_worker.py:63-70 adds ssh_max_sessions to the schema and :14 sets it to 1 in jt-60sa.yaml; the _host_sessions registry sits beside _active_pools; SSHWorkerPool.max_workers = min(max_workers, limit); SSHWorker.start awaits acquire_host_session; executor's four per-call paths take _session_permit and prefer open_worker_pool; the registry docstring states 'One process owns admission... Separate CLI processes do not share these permits.'
item_verdicts.manifest: The reviewed manifest records the three commits, the 58-passed focused gate, the negative control (1 failed, EXIT=1), and the after_suite arm with an absolute-path command; it omits baseline_suite entirely and its baseline.log header is under-specified (see findings).
item_verdicts.write_paths: git diff --stat 5ec8b0ee..a0bbbfc4 touches exactly the manifest's declared paths -- executor.py, ssh_worker.py, tools.py, facility_config.yaml, jt-60sa.yaml, test_ssh_session_limit.py and one docs/evidence fragment -- with no generated or gitignored file staged (the diff --name-only set is exactly those seven).

justifications.durability: Removing the per-call permit in _run_remote_process reddens test_limited_host_serializes_calls_and_unlimited_host_overlaps (1 failed, EXIT=1), reproduced independently in a scratch extraction under TMPDIR. Each assertion compares the observed peak concurrency against an independent expected value (1 for limited, 2 / >=2 for unlimited) measured through real ThreadPoolExecutor and asyncio.gather concurrency rather than a value fed back into the code, and a BoundedSemaphore makes an over-release raise rather than silently widen the bound. Reservation: the synchronous unlimited arm asserts peak == 2 exactly behind a 0.05s sleep, a scheduling race.
justifications.evidence: The gate measures the done-when and the result is recorded: final-absolute-gate.log shows 58 passed, EXIT=0 at a0bbbfc4606bf0e57850f3083f693589eefe9c2e, and the negative control shows 1 failed, EXIT=1. I reproduced the head arm independently (58 passed, EXIT=0, review-head-gate.log), the negative control independently (1 failed, EXIT=1, review-negative-control.log), and confirmed get_facility('jt-60sa')['ssh_max_sessions'] == 1 in three fresh processes. Reservation: the reviewed manifest omits baseline_suite and its baseline.log names base revision 5ec8b0ee while the tree carried intermediate reviewed source -- the true base SOURCE plus the reviewed test is a collection ImportError, so the baseline arm is under-specified.
justifications.fit: The change extends the existing per-host registry idiom: _host_sessions mirrors _host_nice_levels, configure_host_session_limit mirrors configure_host_nice and is registered from the same _resolve_ssh_host path in tools.py, and pool sizing reuses the existing SSHWorkerPool. The process-local scope is stated in the registry docstring, and all three commits carry a conventional subject with a mechanism body and no attribution line. Reservation: executor.py reaches into ssh_worker private names (_session_permit and pool._owner_loop/_started/_closed).
justifications.goal_fidelity: The change implements every element §60 names -- the optional key, the JT-60SA value of 1, one owner beside the pool registry, a pool sized to min(max_workers, limit), one permit per worker for its life, the four per-call paths taking a permit and routing through an open pool, unlimited hosts keeping today's direct behaviour, and the process-local scope stated in the code. No behaviour beyond the section is changed.
justifications.reuse: The change reuses threading.BoundedSemaphore for the bound, the existing _resolve_ssh_host/configure_host_nice registration path in tools.py, the _active_pools WeakSet and its new lock for pool discovery, and SSHWorkerPool.acquire() for the run_subprocess bridge; no second concurrency primitive or duplicate registry is introduced.
justifications.scope_discipline: The reviewed diff 5ec8b0ee..a0bbbfc4 touches exactly the manifest's seven declared paths with a single purpose and stages no generated or gitignored file. The node's fence also named a figures directory, left untouched because the node produced no figure.
